pharm: Anticonvulsant / neuropathic pain agent (Schedule V controlled substance)
quick: Neuropathic pain: start 150 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses; usual 150-300 mg/day
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; possible fetal risk
Present in milk; weigh benefit vs risk, monitor infant
Reduce dose by creatinine clearance - renally eliminated
summary: Pregabalin is a gabapentinoid used for neuropathic pain (diabetic neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, spinal cord injury), fibromyalgia, and as adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures. It is renally cleared (requiring dose reduction in renal impairment), is a Schedule V controlled substance with misuse potential, and can cause sedation, edema, and weight gain.
indications: Neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy
Adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures (patients >=1 month)
Neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury

dosage.d: Start 150 mg/day in 3 divided doses; may increase to 300 mg/day within 1 week
Start 150 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses; titrate to 300 mg/day within 1 week
dosage.n: Max 600 mg/day if needed (in 2-3 divided doses)

dosage.d: Start 150 mg/day in 2 divided doses; titrate to 300 mg/day within 1 week
Start 150 mg/day in 2 divided doses; titrate to 300 mg/day within 1 week
Start 150 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses; titrate to effect
Reduce dose by CrCl (e.g., CrCl 30-60: ~50% of dose; CrCl 15-30: ~25%; CrCl <15: ~1/6); supplemental dose after hemodialysis

admin: Divide total daily dose as specified per indication
Do not stop abruptly - taper over at least 1 week
moa: Binds with high affinity to the alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels in CNS tissues, reducing calcium influx and decreasing release of excitatory neurotransmitters (glutamate, noradrenaline, substance P). It is not a GABA agonist despite structural similarity.
preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Animal data and some registry data suggest possible increased risk of major congenital malformations; counsel and consider safer alternatives where possible.
lact: Excreted into breast milk; a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, weighing benefits. Monitor breastfed infant for sedation and poor feeding.
renal: Renally eliminated essentially unchanged - dose reduction required according to creatinine clearance. Provide a supplementary dose after each hemodialysis session.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed; pregabalin undergoes negligible hepatic metabolism.

major: Opioids (additive CNS/respiratory depression - risk of fatal respiratory depression)
minor: No significant CYP-mediated interactions (not metabolized by CYP enzymes)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive sedation and respiratory depression

monitoring: Sedation and respiratory status (especially with opioids)
counsel: Do not stop suddenly - taper to avoid withdrawal and seizures
Avoid alcohol and be cautious with sedating medicines
May cause dizziness/drowsiness - use care driving until you know its effect
Report swelling, rapid weight gain, mood changes, or breathing problems
This is a controlled medicine - do not share it
pk: Pain relief can begin within the first week of dosing
pearls: Linear, predictable pharmacokinetics (unlike gabapentin) with high oral bioavailability (~90%)
Not metabolized - no CYP interactions; cleared renally
Schedule V controlled substance due to misuse/euphoria potential
Risk of life-threatening respiratory depression when combined with opioids or in respiratory compromise
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and continue the regular schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause somnolence, confusion, agitation, restlessness, and rarely seizures or coma; respiratory depression with co-ingested opioids/CNS depressants. Management is supportive; hemodialysis can remove pregabalin and may be considered in severe renal impairment or large ingestions.
